statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 5 of 100 in the low band, twenty points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 58 in the elevated band on a shut Saudi East-West pipeline, WTI near $100, reported Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 85.6 percent for an increase. Confidence is 86 on a complete verified closing set re-checked this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and the single shared reading applies to each instrument. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about eighteen hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one. Stress remains elevated and is described here as an environment reading only: under the fixed repository mapping it does not alter the mapped state.
headline: A shut weekend tape: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but mid-range, NQ retraced a roughly 459-point round trip after firm core CPI, VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, and an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage, reported Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and Monday's Salalah meeting on Hormuz shipping all travel toward a Sunday reopen that lies beyond this window.
body:
Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. The broader tape agreed, with the Dow up 0.98% to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% to 26,333.04, each snapping a losing streak while still finishing the week lower. VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, closing near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range.

The macro set behind that path is hawkish rather than disorderly. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both matching expectations, with core at 0.3% on the month, one tenth above consensus, and the core annual rate at 2.4% in line. CME FedWatch put the probability of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC at 85.6%, against 48.4% a month earlier. Treasury yields are firm, with the H.15 series showing the 2-year at 4.56%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%. A firm but broadly in-line print that still allowed a 459-point round trip is evidence of orderly price discovery, which is why the event raises Stress and not Tail.

The unresolved risks are in the Gulf and they are supply-route risks. Saudi Arabia shut its 7 million barrel per day East-West pipeline, the route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz toward the Red Sea, after drone attacks Riyadh and Baghdad attributed to Iraqi territory, and no restart date has been announced. Houthi forces completed a push to control Yemen's entire Red Sea coast on Friday, reaching Perim island near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Against that, oil eased rather than extended: WTI settled near $100.05, down 2.37%, and Brent near $104.61, down 2.81%, after Iran said it would meet Gulf foreign ministers and Iraqi representatives in Salalah, Oman on Monday to discuss Hormuz shipping.

Cross-asset context from the shared collector is delayed, latest-session material and is used here as confirmation only, never as live price-path evidence. Its section coverage was partial this hour, with the calendar feed unavailable, so the calendar below rests on independently verified sources. What it does show is that Friday's advance was broad but internally dispersed: seven of eight tracked megacaps higher with a mean gain near 0.94%, semiconductors uneven with ARM up 4.17%, QCOM up 2.88% and NVDA fractionally lower, and Treasury futures modestly lower in line with firm yields. Dispersion of that kind is the opposite of the single-direction alignment that precedes mean-reversion failure.

The decisive fact for this horizon is mechanical. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about eighteen hours after the last slot of this forecast. Every one of the twenty-four forward hours therefore describes a market in which no Nasdaq-100 price can print, so no persistent one-way path, no failed retracement and no session extreme can form. Conditional Tail is held at a low residual floor that steps from 5 to 10 across the horizon, tracking accumulated unpriced weekend headline exposure ahead of an eventual reopen rather than any observed structure. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 05:00 UTC on 11 September to 04:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at Tail 11 in mixed mode during the Asian session, then firms into a trend-up read between 06:00 and 11:00 UTC with Tail between 13 and 15 as European hours extended the advance. The 12:30 UTC inflation print produced the only elevated readings of the window, Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail then fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, and collapsed to 13 and then 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final seven slots sit at Tail 5 to 6 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 86 to 58 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about eighteen hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 5 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, holds that residual floor through the early Saturday hours, then steps to 6 from 08:00 UTC, 7 from 14:00 UTC, 8 from 20:00 UTC, 9 from 00:00 UTC on Sunday and 10 in the final slot as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout. Stress runs 58 to 62 and describes the environment rather than a path: a shut Saudi East-West pipeline with no restart date, WTI near $100.05, reported Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, Monday's Salalah meeting on Hormuz shipping and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 85.6 percent for an increase. Confidence decays gently from 86 to 78 as the verified evidence set ages without any live price path to refresh it. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.
